text:
hana (compliance): Auditor asked for a formal chain-of-custody bundle for the emergency RBAC change during the 2026-03-15 incident — can we assemble artifacts and a control map for SOC2/ISO?

mike (oncall): pinging @rami @olivia — which logs + artifacts show who approved, who made the change, and KMS usage? :thinking_face:

rami (secops): We have three canonical sources: Jira approval comment (JIRA-4412), Vault approval audit (vault.audit), and CloudTrail KMS events. I can pull a timeline of Decrypt/Encrypt calls and IAM role modifications.

mike (oncall): FYI the RBAC change was a temporary RoleBinding for `service-account:incident-runner` in `prod` for ~2h. I can confirm exact start/end timestamps.

olivia (engops): I'll stage an evidence folder and create a presigned zip. Path I plan: s3://redwood-evidence/6843219999/incident-2026-03-15/ — will redact IPs and session tokens per policy.

auditor_jane: We also need proof that keys used to decrypt logs weren’t exported or used outside of the approved flow — include KMS key policy snapshot, key rotation state, and Decrypt call details.

rami (secops): CloudTrail shows `Decrypt` calls tied to the service principal used by the oncall runner and to an ops account. I'll export matching CT entries and the KMS DescribeKey JSON. If the auditor wants envelope metadata (KeyWrap) we can include that too. @hana any HSM attestation required?

hana (compliance): HSM attestation isn't necessary for SOC2, but include: key rotation schedule export, alias->key-id mapping, and KMS policy at the time of the incident. Also include RBAC diffs from GitOps (pre/post PR). Map artifacts to CC6.2 / A.9.1 in a one-line narrative per artifact.

mike (oncall): copying the exact command used in the incident for traceability:
```
kubectl create rolebinding emergency-incident-runner --clusterrole=view --serviceaccount=prod:incident-runner --namespace=prod
```

olivia (engops): I'll snapshot the GitOps PR and commit: `git@repo:infra/k8s-configs@pr/412` and export the diff. Will save as `pr-412-diff.patch`.

evidence-bot: packaging started — files added to staging: `cloudtrail-kms-6843219999.ndjson`, `jira-4412.pdf`, `pr-412-diff.patch`, `kms-describe-rlw-prod-logs.json`. Current zip size 12MB.

auditor_jane: Please include a short manifest that maps each artifact to the specific control/test (e.g., "cloudtrail-kms-*.ndjson -> CC6.2: crypto key usage audit"), and a signed chain-of-custody listing personnel who handled artifacts.

hana (compliance): will draft the mapping and manifest. Also need timestamped approval evidence — the Slack thread reaction + the Jira approval comment. @mike can you confirm you reacted?

mike (oncall): I reacted :thumbsup: at 6843220123 (during the incident). Ticket comment included an explicit "approved" by me.

rami (secops): exported and sanitized CloudTrail and KMS entries; uploaded to the evidence folder. Presigned link will be posted once the full bundle is ready.

olivia (engops): KMS metadata saved via `aws kms describe-key --key-id alias/rlw-prod-logs` -> `kms-describe-rlw-prod-logs.json`. Also exported `aws kms get-key-rotation-status --key-id ...` output.

auditor_jane: One final ask: the manifest should include SHA256 checksums, storage path, who pulled the data, and any redactions (fields removed and why). That's required for our audit trail.

hana (compliance): noted. I'll assemble the manifest with checksums and redaction notes, and sign it off. Expect initial draft in this thread in ~30m.

mike (oncall): thanks all — once @auditor_jane confirms receipt of the bundle & manifest we can close JIRA-4412.

evidence-bot: package complete — presigned URL (expires in 7d): <redacted-presigned-url> — manifest `coc-manifest-6843219999.json` included.
